name: Transport authority network administration
one_line: J-DEPTH placeholder template on the fieldless government schema for the authority-side record of specifying, publishing, ordering, and maintaining a public transport or highway NETWORK: machine-readable service and fare feeds and the scheduling exports behind them, service specifications under a contracted or franchised operator, traffic regulation and road-space orders, street-works noticing registers, standing asset and structure inspection registers, count and collision datasets, and the operational telemetry beside them. It is not activated by a transport organisation's name, a transport industry, a journey, a ticket, a vehicle document, or a downloaded timetable. It differs from the government default template by recognizing published network artefacts whose structure is the evidence, and by carrying a split privacy posture the default does not have: deliberately-open feed files sit beside movement traces of members of the public who never filed, applied, bid, or corresponded.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: the government schema declares no field rows, so nothing below licenses a route, mode, asset, order, or operator fact. Every signal must evidence the holder as the NETWORK-OWNING or NETWORK-SPECIFYING authority, not merely as a transport organisation, an operator, or a traveller.

a transit feed package whose members are the fixed named tables of a public transport interchange format — an archive containing agency, stops, routes, trips, stop_times, and calendar members, or an XML document whose root and profile elements declare a scheduled-service exchange schema — held together with the authority-side publication apparatus for it (an unpublished or draft revision, a scheduling-system export, a validator error report for the holder's own release, or a dated release series of the same feed)

a service specification or service-level annex under a contracted, franchised, or concessioned operator, with labelled slots for route or contract-package identity, service pattern and frequency, first and last departure, vehicle or accessibility requirement, and a punctuality or reliability regime, plus an authority issuer block; the operator's bid response to the same specification is excluded by holder role

a fares and ticketing instrument on the authority side: a fare table or fare-revision schedule with labelled product, zone or band, and concession-entitlement columns, or a fare-change order or determination with an effective-date slot and an authorizing-office block

a traffic regulation, road-space, or network order in its authority-side form — a draft or sealed order with a schedule of restrictions, an accompanying statement of reasons, a notice of proposal, an objection register, and a making or sealing block; a copy of the same order downloaded by an objector or a resident does not satisfy the role precondition

a street-works or road-space noticing register whose rows carry a works or permit reference, promoter, road or section identity, permit or notice category, start and end dates, and condition or inspection outcome columns, held as the coordinating authority's own operational register rather than as one promoter's application

a standing asset or structure register and its cyclical inspection record: an inventory keyed by an asset or structure identifier with condition-score, defect, inspection-cycle, and next-due columns, or an inspection report repeating that identifier against a prior inspection of the SAME standing asset with no construction contract attached

a network measurement or safety dataset produced or commissioned by the authority: automatic count or classified-count output with site reference, interval, direction, and class columns, a journey-time or punctuality return keyed by route and period, or a collision or casualty record keyed by an incident reference with location, severity, and vehicle or casualty attribute columns

an operational telemetry or ticketing export carrying the authority's own system provenance — vehicle-location or automatic-vehicle-location traces, smartcard or account-based ticketing transaction extracts, enforcement camera evidence registers, or passenger counting extracts — recognized from structured system metadata and column headers, and treated as protected on sight

a network export or scheduling archive manifest whose paths repeatedly encode one contract package, one order, one feed release, one asset register, or one measurement round together with the authority's own system or custodian metadata; manifests are inspected without unpacking

a transport-office email or calendar record whose structured sender, recipient, organizer, attendee, subject, attachment, and reference slots tie it to an already evidenced authority-side network workflow such as a timetable change round, an order consultation, a works coordination meeting, or an inspection programme; an authority mail domain alone never fires
needs_llm: deciding HOLDER ROLE when identical network bytes may sit with the specifying authority, the contracted operator, a works promoter or utility, an app or data developer who downloaded the open feed, a consultant, a campaigner, or a passenger; interpretation may use only a bounded local dossier and must abstain when custody is unresolved

separating the authority that specifies and owns the network from a commercially-run operator, a state-owned transport company, an infrastructure concessionaire, a bus or rail industry association, or a mobility platform whose branding and statutory language overlap

deciding whether a standing-asset inspection belongs to a live construction or refurbishment contract (a handover or defects record) or to a cyclical asset-management programme on an already-owned structure
deciding whether a road-space document is a case decision about one named applicant or an instrument that changes the network for everyone; the same file family contains both
recognizing an unlabeled timetable-change options paper, network review, service-reduction rationale, or bus-priority scheme note whose function is expressed only in prose
deciding whether a feed archive or dataset is the holder's own publication run or a third party's download of the same published bytes
judging whether a mixed transport packet is authority-side network administration or a traveller's, employee's, or enthusiast's collection of tickets, timetables, vehicle documents, and photographs
interpreting multilingual or non-Latin-script network orders, notices, and fare tables whose labelled role vocabulary is not covered by deterministic structure rules
abstaining whenever the evidence cannot cite an authority-side network role; “A model that cannot cite sufficient evidence must return unknown.”
never_alone: a transit agency, transport department, highways authority, port, airport, railway, metro, or bus operator name, logo, roundel, livery, or seal alone; the entity may be publisher, operator, employer, counterparty, subject, or the service the holder merely rides

a downloaded published feed, timetable, network map, fares leaflet, service-change notice, or open-data extract with no authority-side publication apparatus beside it; publication by a transport authority is not authority-side custody — this is the row's principal false positive

route, service, line, mode, station, stop, corridor, carriageway, junction, timetable, fare, zone, permit, order, or asset vocabulary alone; these are topic words and, in the operator's and the traveller's worlds, the same words describe entirely different holdings

a traveller's ticket, season pass, smartcard statement, booking confirmation, boarding pass, journey history, refund claim, or delay-repay correspondence; the holder is the passenger and finance, identity, Receipts and Confirmations, or Independent Records owns it

a person's or firm's vehicle registration, roadworthiness certificate, driving licence, operator licence, tachograph record, penalty notice, or bus-lane charge received; a transport authority issued it, but the recipient's copy never activates this row
an operator's own depot roster, crew diagram, fleet maintenance record, fuel return, or tender response, even when it quotes the authority's specification verbatim; role, not vocabulary, decides
a geospatial file, shapefile, GeoJSON, GPX trace, routing-engine extract, or crowd-mapped network dump alone; a network geometry is not proof that an authority produced or owns it

a file extension or source_type alone, including the interchange-format extensions this row leans on; the design says to “treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning”
a parent folder named Transport, Transit, Highways, Network, Timetables, Fleet, or Roads alone
a bulk open-data harvest or portal download batch; “A session should never be treated as proof of topic”
missing EXIF or dense OCR as proof that an image is a departure-board or works-notice capture; “the system must not mistake the absence of EXIF for proof that an image is a screenshot”

the presence of an openly published feed or map in a folder as grounds for lowering the posture of a ticketing, telemetry, enforcement, or casualty file beside it; open network data and re-identifying movement data routinely share one directory

work_types: network or service plan, service review, corridor study, or timetable-change options paper
service specification, service-level annex, contract-package schedule, or operator performance regime under a franchise or concession
timetable production, scheduling export, feed release, feed revision, or feed validation record
fare table, fare revision schedule, concession-entitlement rule, or fare determination
traffic regulation order, road-space order, temporary restriction, diversion order, statement of reasons, notice of proposal, or objection register
street-works or road-space noticing, permit coordination register, works inspection, or defect-notice record
asset and structure inventory, condition survey, cyclical or principal inspection, defect register, or maintenance programme
traffic count, classified count, journey-time survey, punctuality or reliability return, or passenger counting output
collision, casualty, incident, or safety-scheme record on the authority side
ticketing, smartcard, or account-based fare-collection operational extract
vehicle-location, telemetry, real-time information, or service-disruption operational record
service-change consultation, network consultation, or works notification to the public
passenger, resident, or objector casework held by the transport office
accessibility, bus-priority, active-travel, or safety scheme design, delivery, monitoring, and evaluation record
grouping_reasons: one evidenced network instrument lifecycle, linked by an exact order, scheme, or determination reference across proposal notice, schedule of restrictions, statement of reasons, objections, and the made instrument

one contract package or franchise, linking service specification versions, variation instructions, performance returns, and payment or deduction schedules by an exact package reference, without copying the package label onto a sparse member

one feed release series, linking a scheduling export, draft revision, validation report, and published package by an exact feed or release identifier; the release is a version family, not a new network fact
one standing asset or structure, linking successive cyclical inspections, defect records, and condition scores by an exact asset or structure identifier; a repeat inspection is not a new asset
one street-works or road-space coordination round, linking notices, permits, conditions, and inspection outcomes by an exact works reference
one measurement or safety round, linking instrument, site or incident references, raw extract, quality note, and published output while raw and published members retain different access boundaries
one passenger, resident, or objector case, but only inside a protected, locally processed group with exact case anchors and no cross-person semantic joining
one network export or scheduling archive manifest, kept shallow until access boundaries are known and never unpacked merely to strengthen recognition
duplicate and version families remain universal relationships; repeated timetables, fare tables, order drafts, and inspection templates do not acquire new government facts from neighborhood context

no group is a valid outcome for a standalone published notice, map, timetable, or fares leaflet; “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”

template.why: Empty by contract, and this is the one node-test leg on which this row does NOT differ from its schema default: PR-6 leaves the government schema fieldless and a template cannot branch on undeclared fields, so both this row and the government default template recommend nothing. The prose shape is nonetheless distinct and is recorded for later adjudication: the organizing anchor is the network object or bounded instrument — contract package, order, standing asset, feed release, or measurement round — then the exact reference, then function, then time. Named passengers, objectors, and casualties must never become the organizing dimension. Time is not first because “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.” — a timetable folder ordered by year would split one route's specification, its orders, and its inspections across a decade of calendar folders. Any later order remains editable because “The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions.”

collides_with.signal: One archive, Bus Service Contract Package 12 - Invitation to Tender and Evaluation.zip, is contested member by member. Public procurement owns the competition lifecycle — notice, bidder responses, evaluation matrix, declared interests, award recommendation. This row owns the service specification that outlives the award and is varied for years afterwards. A standalone Service Specification - Contract Package 12 - Route 42 - v7.docx with a variation table and no competition is this row; the evaluation matrix inside the same zip is never this row.

Both worlds hold road-space paperwork. Permit-licensing owns the case-by-case decision about one named applicant, with applicant slots, conditions, reasons, and an appeal route. This row owns the instrument that changes the network for everyone and the coordinating register that spans many promoters. Street Works Permit Register - August 2026.csv is this row because its rows carry many different promoters and a coordination custodian; one promoter's permit application with a decision and reasons is permit-licensing even when the works are on a highway, and TRO 2026-11 is this row rather than permit-licensing because it decides nothing about an applicant.

Highways and Transport Committee - Agenda Pack - 18 August 2026.pdf is claimed by both. Municipal administration owns the governance cycle — agenda, numbered papers, attendance, minute, resolution — whatever the subject matter, and the pack is therefore municipal. This row owns the network artefact an annex summarizes; the standing bridge condition register the annex is drawn from is this row, and municipal administration must not absorb it merely because a committee once received a summary of it.

Passenger complaint 8841 - missed connection and refund.eml is contested. Constituent casework owns a named person's case held by a public office, and that email is casework. This row owns the aggregate service record the complaint is measured against — the punctuality return and the performance regime in the specification. Casework must not claim the route-level performance return, and this row must not claim the individual's case file merely because the subject is a bus.

Structure B-114 - Principal Inspection 2026 - condition record.pdf sits on the seam. Construction-project owns inspection and condition evidence attached to a live build or refurbishment contract — handover packs, defects liability, valuations, final account. This row owns cyclical inspection of a standing asset the authority already owns, evidenced by an inspection cycle, a next-due date, a comparison to a prior inspection of the same structure identifier, and the absence of any contract or valuation reference. The same structure moves between the two rows over its life, and the discriminator is the contract, not the structure.

Depot duty roster and fleet defect log - week 32.xlsx quotes this row's specification verbatim yet is not this row. Business operations owns the transport company's own operating record — rosters, fleet maintenance, fuel, bids, depot administration. This row requires the specifying or network-owning authority as holder. The identical punctuality return is business operations in the operator's hands and this row in the authority's; nothing in the bytes decides it, only custody.

Both worlds hold bridge documents. Engineering civil-structural owns the design analysis — loading assumptions, calculations, capacity assessment, design drawings. This row owns the owner's condition and inventory record. For Structure B-114 the calculation sheet is engineering and the cyclical condition record with defect scoring is this row; neither may infer the other's conclusion, and this row must never assert that a structure is safe or load-capable.

falls_through_to.when: a readable standalone published timetable, network map, fares leaflet, works notice, made order, or inspection certificate has durable value but no authority-side network workflow or accepted neighboring group
falls_through_to.design_cite: Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.

falls_through_to.when: ticketing, telemetry, enforcement, casualty, casework, objector, or bidder material lacks a safe accepted domain group, including anything that reconstructs an identifiable person's movements
falls_through_to.design_cite: Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.

falls_through_to.when: a downloaded open feed, published dataset, transport strategy, consultation report, or research paper is held for reading or reuse rather than as authority-side network work
falls_through_to.design_cite: Reading Inbox may hold papers, articles, reports, and saved PDFs that appear to be reading material but have no active research, course, or project association.

falls_through_to.when: the artefact is structurally a network instrument, feed, or specification but the holder role — authority, operator, promoter, consultant, or data consumer — cannot be settled safely
falls_through_to.design_cite: Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.

falls_through_to.when: a scheduling-system binary, encrypted telemetry export, proprietary asset-database dump, or damaged feed archive cannot yield evidence beyond metadata
falls_through_to.design_cite: Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.

falls_through_to.when: a positively evidenced screen capture of a departure board, works notice, journey planner, or portal does not establish an accepted authority-side workflow
falls_through_to.design_cite: Temporary Screenshots may live under Photos/Temporary Screenshots and hold screenshots that appear time-sensitive or remind the user of something but have no accepted project, trip, application, or event relationship.

sensitivity_why: This row's privacy problem is different in kind from the government default's, and that difference is one of the two legs on which it earns node status. The default schema's sensitive material concerns people who interacted with the authority — applicants, requesters, bidders, casework subjects, respondents. Here the most re-identifying holdings concern people who did nothing but travel: smartcard and account-based ticketing extracts that reconstruct daily movement, vehicle-location and passenger-counting traces, enforcement camera packages with readable plates, and casualty records with age and injury attributes. A pseudonymous card token is not anonymity. The second difference is a split posture inside one directory: deliberately-published feeds, maps, and made orders sit beside those extracts, and the presence of open data must never lower the posture of what is next to it. The design requires: “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector.” It further says protected material “should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it.”
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH: (a) PR-6 keeps government fieldless, so the network anchor concepts this row would organize on — a bounded instrument or contract-package reference, a standing asset identifier, and a feed release identifier — are proposed as prose only; decide centrally whether any authority-side anchor field may exist and whether it is destination-eligible. (b) Decide whether a published open feed inside an authority corpus may ever be marked non-sensitive independently of its neighbours, or whether directory-level posture always dominates. (c) Decide the holder-role rule for a state-owned or arm's-length transport company that both specifies and operates the network, where the authority and operator seam this row relies on does not exist.
